question.worked_solution:
First, let's try direct substitution:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to (\pi /8)^{+}}\operatorname{tan}⁡(4x) & ={lim}_{x\to (\pi /8)^{+}}\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(4x)}{\operatorname{cos}⁡(4x)} \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(4\cdot \frac{\pi }{8})}{\operatorname{cos}⁡(4\cdot \frac{\pi }{8})} \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})}{\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})} \\  & =\frac{1}{0},\end{aligned}
$$

which is not defined.

Therefore, to find the limit, let's sketch the graph of $y=\operatorname{tan}⁡(4x).$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14258704/assets/60d8281e4b2655ebb054a54616b4e034be1bda60579db8b565346275d68acc11.png)

We see that as $x$ approaches $\frac{\pi }{8}$ from the right, the values of $y=\operatorname{tan}⁡(4x)$ are negative and decrease without bound. Therefore, we conclude that

$$
{lim}_{x\to (\pi /8)^{+}}\operatorname{tan}⁡(4x)=-\infty .
$$
